thread.title: Exactly When Will Shares Of Applied Materials Bottom? - Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT)

author: Chris Lau
title: Exactly When Will Shares Of Applied Materials Bottom? - Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT)
text:
Applied Materials ( AMAT ) is not finding many stock buyers in light of the bearishness for semiconductor stocks. Investors are expecting a tougher second half of the year as memory and storage prices drop. At the macro level, trade tensions have a high chance of the U.S. adding even more tariffs against China. With the stock valued at 8 times current and forward P/E multiples, does the stock price discount enough of the uncertainties that lie ahead?
AMAT reported double-digit growth in its major businesses but management forecasted a 2H/2019 recovery. Near term, the industry faces macro-level uncertainties. Lower investments in memory in the industry, trade tensions between the U.S. and China, and softer chip pricing are all hurting prospects today. In 2019, revenue could fall as much as 20% year-on-year, suggesting that the forward 8x P/E will go up by a few points and narrow the implied stock discount.
Investors may look at historical chip cycles to estimate AMAT’s downside, but the company is healthier than ever. It has a new playbook that includes the development of new chip architecture, new 3D structures within a chip, and new, innovative ways to connect chips together. The macro headwind from trade disruptions will hurt revenue in the next two quarters but AMAT will continue its pace of R&D spend. The long-term bodes well even as uncertainties rise.
Strong Fourth Quarter Results Applied ended the quarter with $5.6 billion in cash as operating cash flow rose 27% Y/Y to $1.1 billion. Management put the cash to work by buying back $751 million worth of shares. The downside of this purchase is that it bought the stock at higher prices.
2019 – 2020 Outlook Looking ahead, AMAT forecasts revenue of $3.56 billion - $3.86 billion. Service revenue will rise by 7% and revenue from Display will increase by 10%. Non-GAAP EPS will be as high as $0.83 a share. Looking beyond the quarter and into 2020, Applied has new products that will support growth. The 3D NAND product is a 2020 growth story just as it is for Micron Technology ( MU ). Admittedly, spending for 3D NAND is on the downtrend and will not recover until later. AMAT stock is a more compelling rebound play because the company forecasts a 2019 recovery is more likely with the foundry segment , followed by logic and then DRAM and NAND. The view that NAND is the weakest of the four markets is consistent with that of Western Digital ( WDC ) warning on its conference call that demand is weak and pricing is soft.
AMAT data by YCharts The Display unit will fall by around 15% – 20% in 2019. Offsetting the elevated downside risk is TV makers transitioning to Gen 10.5 technology, which brings lower costs for large screen TVs. Just as Apple ( AAPL ) suppliers like LG Display ( LPL ), Lumentum ( LITE ) and Skyworks ( SWKS ) confirming supply order cuts on weak smartphone demand, Applied Materials also forecasts flat revenue. Management still views an OLED recovery if suppliers improve on yield.
LITE data by YCharts Note: Investors interested in OLED suppliers should watch Universal Display Corporation ( OLED ). The company is a researcher in OLED technologies. The stock topped $209 earlier this year but now trades at a still-expensive 14.4 times sales.
Timing the Inflection Point Applied’s management thinks it's more conservative to forecast a first-half 2019 recovery than to expect a rebound this coming January. The U-shaped recovery will probably be more shallow and gradual than in the past. This outlook may be more pessimistic than necessary. Services grew 25% year-on-year but management is guiding lower for January.
Valuation Investors should forecast a conservative EBIT Margin in the range of 10% - 30% and a cost of capital of around 10%. An Earnings Power Value model would suggest the stock now trades at fair value.

Your Takeaway Applied Materials survived a deep and prolonged selloff when regulators rejected its merger with an Asian firm. This time around, the downside is driven by macro unknowns. Eventually, the countries must speak openly to re-establish open trade. If that happens, the supply chain for semiconductors will raise capital expenditure levels, ultimately ending the downtrend in shares of Applied Materials.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
